questions.question: What gets bigger the more you take away from it?
questions.fact: Every spadeful you take out of a hole makes it bigger. A debt, a pile of sand or a cake all shrink when you take from them.

questions.question: What has a neck and wears a cap, but has no head?
questions.fact: A bottle has a narrow neck and a cap on top, but no head. Snakes have heads, rivers have mouths and shirts have collars, not caps.

questions.question: What has two hands and a face but no arms?
questions.fact: A clock face has an hour hand and a minute hand. A chair is the trap: it has arms, and a tree has branches, not hands.

questions.question: What has one eye but can't see anything?
questions.fact: The hole you thread at the top of a sewing needle is called its eye. Buttons have holes too, but nobody calls them eyes.

questions.question: What has lots of teeth but never bites?
questions.fact: The thin prongs of a comb are called teeth, but they only bite into tangles. Riddles like this play on a word having two meanings.

questions.question: What goes up but never comes down?
questions.fact: Your age only ever goes up, one birthday at a time. Lifts, kites and thrown balls all come back down sooner or later.

questions.question: What can you catch but never throw?
questions.fact: You catch a cold, but you can't throw one to somebody else on purpose. Balls, frisbees and wedding bouquets are all made for throwing.

questions.question: What is full of holes but still holds water?
questions.fact: A sponge is full of tiny holes that soak up water and hold it. A bucket has no holes, while a net and a sieve let the water out.

questions.question: What has to be broken before you can use it?
questions.fact: You have to crack an egg before you can cook it. Windows, mirrors and clocks are useless once they're broken.

questions.question: The more of these you take, the more you leave behind. What are they?
questions.fact: Every step you take leaves a footstep behind you, so the more you take, the more you leave. Biscuits, sadly, just disappear.

questions.question: What belongs to you, but other people use it more than you do?
questions.fact: Your name is yours, but everyone else says it far more often than you do. Hopefully nobody else uses your toothbrush.

questions.question: What runs but never walks, and has a mouth but never talks?
questions.fact: A river runs downhill and ends at its mouth, where it meets the sea. A tap runs but has no mouth, and a dog walks.

questions.question: What has a thumb and four fingers but isn't alive?
questions.fact: A glove has a thumb and four fingers but nothing inside unless you wear it. A fork and a rake have prongs, and a sock has no fingers.

questions.question: What goes up when the rain comes down?
questions.fact: The moment it starts raining, umbrellas go up. Kites, deckchairs and sunhats all get packed away instead.

questions.question: I'm tall when I'm young and short when I'm old. What am I?
questions.fact: A new candle is tall, and it gets shorter as it burns down. Trees and giraffes grow taller with age, and towers stay the same.

questions.question: What can travel around the world while staying in one corner?
questions.fact: A stamp sits in the corner of an envelope and can travel all the way around the world. A suitcase travels too, but has no corner to stay in.

questions.question: What comes next: 2, 4, 8, 16, ...?
questions.fact: Each number is double the one before it, so after 16 comes 16 x 2 = 32.

questions.question: What comes next: 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, ...?
questions.fact: These are the square numbers: 1x1, 2x2, 3x3, 4x4 and 5x5. The next one is 6 x 6 = 36.

questions.question: A farmer has 17 sheep. All but 9 run away. How many sheep are left?
questions.fact: "All but 9" means every sheep except 9 ran away, so 9 are left. The trap is to work out 17 - 9 = 8.

questions.question: Say "silk" five times in your head. Now: what do cows drink?
questions.fact: Cows drink water. Cows make milk, but repeating "silk" primes your brain to blurt out the rhyming word.

questions.question: What walks on four legs in the morning, two at noon and three in the evening?
questions.fact: A baby crawls on all fours, an adult walks on two legs and an old person uses a stick. In Greek myth this was the Sphinx's riddle, solved by Oedipus.

questions.question: What can fill a whole room but takes up no space?
questions.fact: Light can fill a room from wall to wall without taking up any space. Water, furniture and balloons all take up space.

questions.question: I have cities but no houses, forests but no trees and water but no fish. What am I?
questions.fact: A map shows cities, forests and seas, but there are no real houses, trees or fish on it, just symbols and colours.

questions.question: What starts with T, ends with T and has T in it?
questions.fact: "Teapot" starts and ends with the letter T, and it has tea in it. Only teapot ends in T among the options.

questions.question: A rooster lays an egg on top of a pointed roof. Which way does the egg roll?
questions.fact: Roosters are male chickens, so they don't lay eggs at all. Only hens do. The roof details are there to get you thinking about angles.

questions.question: What can you hold without ever touching it?
questions.fact: You can hold your breath without touching anything. A pen, a rope and a door all have to be gripped to be held.

questions.question: What comes once in a minute, twice in a moment, but never in a thousand years?
questions.fact: "Minute" has one M, "moment" has two and "a thousand years" has none. The letter E fails because "a thousand years" has one.

questions.question: Which word is always spelled wrong in every dictionary?
questions.fact: The answer is the word "wrong" itself: every dictionary spells it W-R-O-N-G. All the other words are spelled correctly there.

questions.question: Forwards I'm heavy, but backwards I'm not. What am I?
questions.fact: A ton is heavy, and "ton" spelled backwards is "not". Lead, rock and iron backwards give "dael", "kcor" and "nori".

questions.question: Which word gets shorter when you add two letters to it?
questions.fact: Add "er" to "short" and you get "shorter". The other words turn into "longer", "taller" and "wider".

questions.question: What comes next: 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, ...?
questions.fact: Each number is the sum of the two before it, so 5 + 8 = 13. This is the Fibonacci sequence, named after the Italian mathematician who wrote about it in 1202.

questions.question: What comes next: 3, 6, 11, 18, 27, ...?
questions.fact: The gaps grow by 2 each time: +3, +5, +7, +9, so the next gap is +11 and 27 + 11 = 38.

questions.question: What comes next: 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, ...?
questions.fact: These are the prime numbers, which divide only by 1 and themselves. The next prime after 11 is 13. 12 and 15 aren't prime.

questions.question: What letter comes next: J, F, M, A, M, J, ...?
questions.fact: These are the first letters of the months: January to June. Next comes July, so the answer is J.

questions.question: A bat and a ball cost €1.10. The bat costs €1 more than the ball. How much is the ball?
questions.fact: Ball 5 cents + bat €1.05 = €1.10. If the ball were 10 cents, the bat would be €1.10 and the total €1.20. From a famous 2005 reasoning test.

questions.question: In a race, you overtake the person in second place. What place are you in now?
questions.fact: You took second place from them, so now you're second. To be first you'd have to overtake the person in the lead.

questions.question: A doctor gives you 3 pills and says take one every half hour. How long do they last?
questions.fact: Take the first pill now, the second after 30 minutes and the last after 60 minutes. So they're gone in 1 hour, not 90 minutes.

questions.question: How many animals of each kind did Moses take on the Ark?
questions.fact: In the Bible it was Noah who built the Ark, not Moses. Psychologists call missing this the "Moses illusion".

questions.question: A dark drawer has black socks and white socks. How many must you take out to be sure of a pair?
questions.fact: There are only two colours. Two socks could be one of each, but a third sock must match one of them.

questions.question: Mary's father has five daughters: Nana, Nene, Nini and Nono. What's the fifth daughter called?
questions.fact: The question starts with Mary's father, so Mary herself is the fifth daughter. The pattern of names is there to lead you to "Nunu".

questions.question: A plane crashes right on the border of France and Spain. Where do they bury the survivors?
questions.fact: Survivors are alive, so nobody buries them. Your brain is busy with the border question and skips the word "survivors".

questions.question: A house has all four walls facing south. A bear walks past. What colour is the bear?
questions.fact: Only at the North Pole does every direction point south, so the house must be in the Arctic, where the bears are white polar bears.

questions.question: What do you get if you add up every whole number from 1 to 100?
questions.fact: Pair them up: 1 + 100, 2 + 99 and so on makes 50 pairs of 101, which is 5050. The mathematician Gauss reportedly did this as a schoolboy.

questions.question: Which is correct: "The yolk of the egg is white" or "The yolk of the egg are white"?
questions.fact: Egg yolks are yellow, so neither sentence is true. The grammar question is a distraction from the facts.

questions.question: Voiceless it cries, wingless flutters, toothless bites, mouthless mutters. What is it?
questions.fact: The wind howls, flaps things, bites with cold and mutters through cracks. Gollum asks Bilbo this riddle in Tolkien's The Hobbit.

questions.question: A box without hinges, key or lid, yet golden treasure inside is hid. What is it?
questions.fact: An egg has no hinges, key or lid, and its golden treasure is the yolk. Bilbo asks Gollum this one in Tolkien's The Hobbit.

questions.question: What is so fragile that just saying its name breaks it?
questions.fact: The moment you say "silence", you've broken the silence. You can say the word "secret" or "glass" without breaking anything.

questions.question: Poor people have it, rich people need it, and if you eat it you'll die. What is it?
questions.fact: Poor people have nothing, rich people need nothing, and if you eat nothing for long enough, you die. Money and poison fail the other clues.

questions.question: I'm an odd number. Take away one letter and I become even. What number am I?
questions.fact: Take the S off "seven" and you get "even". No single letter can be removed from nine, eleven or three to spell "even".

questions.question: Which three whole numbers give the same answer whether you add them or multiply them?
questions.fact: 1 + 2 + 3 = 6 and 1 x 2 x 3 = 6. For 2, 2, 2 you get 6 and 8, for 1, 1, 2 you get 4 and 2, and for 1, 3, 4 you get 8 and 12.

questions.question: A woman shoots her husband, holds him underwater, then hangs him up. Later they go to dinner. How?
questions.fact: She took his photo, developed it in a tray of liquid and hung it up to dry, as in an old darkroom. A classic lateral-thinking puzzle.

questions.question: A man pushes his car to a hotel and tells the owner he's bankrupt. Why?
questions.fact: In Monopoly you move your car token, land on a hotel you can't pay for and go bankrupt. Nothing about a real car or real hotel.

questions.question: Two fathers and two sons go fishing. Each catches one fish, and they catch 3 fish in total. How?
questions.fact: They're a grandfather, a father and a son. The middle one is both a father and a son, so 3 people make two fathers and two sons.

questions.question: What letter comes next: O, T, T, F, F, S, S, ...?
questions.fact: They're the first letters of One, Two, Three, Four, Five, Six, Seven. Next is Eight, so the answer is E.

questions.question: What comes next: 1, 11, 21, 1211, 111221, ...?
questions.fact: Each term describes the one before: 111221 is "three 1s, two 2s, one 1", written 312211. The mathematician John Conway studied this "look-and-say" sequence.

questions.question: How many squares of any size are there on a chessboard?
questions.fact: Count each size: 64 (1x1) + 49 + 36 + 25 + 16 + 9 + 4 + 1 (the whole board) = 204. The 64 small squares are only the start.

questions.question: A snail climbs 3 m up a 10 m well each day and slips 2 m back each night. On which day does it get out?
questions.fact: It gains 1 m per day and night, so after 7 days it's at 7 m. On day 8 it climbs 3 m, reaches the top and never slips back.

questions.question: A clock takes 5 seconds to strike 6 o'clock. How long does it take to strike 12 o'clock?
questions.fact: 6 strikes have 5 gaps between them, so each gap is 1 second. 12 strikes have 11 gaps, which take 11 seconds.

questions.question: 5 machines make 5 widgets in 5 minutes. How long do 100 machines take to make 100 widgets?
questions.fact: Each machine makes one widget in 5 minutes, so 100 machines make 100 widgets in the same 5 minutes. From a famous 2005 reasoning test.

questions.question: Lily pads double in area every day and cover a whole lake on day 48. On which day was it half covered?
questions.fact: Because the patch doubles every day, it was half the size the day before it covered the lake: day 47. Day 24 is the tempting wrong answer.
